verdict: OK to lend in Mohali tractors & farm machinery — back proven component and implement suppliers to the Swaraj anchor, structure tightly on receivables and inventory, and decline new exposure to pure dealer/seasonal buyers with weak balance sheets.
title: Mohali tractors & farm machinery: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A tractor or farm-machinery unit in Mohali turns steel, castings, hydraulics and bought-out aggregates into machines and spares, and gets paid after the dealer or OEM chain clears.** Mohali's major industries include tractors and engineering goods, and the district houses around 30 large-scale industries with turnover above Rs.250 crore, including Swaraj Tractors [1]. The district carries over 71,126 MSMEs [1], so most of our book here will be tier-2 and tier-3 suppliers, job-workers and dealers feeding that anchor, not the OEM itself. Cash sits in inventory (castings, aggregates, finished machines) and in receivables from OEMs and dealers; value sits in the OEM approval, the tooling and the service relationship, not in the shed. ## What has changed now
**National demand signals are positive but the local policy picture is stale and unresolved.** India-wide IIP for NIC 28 output is +10.3% YoY and +10.4% Apr-to-date [D], and Punjab GST collections are +9.7% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D]. **Treat the local news as dated context, not current fact; the demand read comes from [D] and peers.** Peer results are mixed-to-firm: Escorts Kubota posted a 9.2% rise in Q4 profit on higher tractor sales [5][6], while a CRISIL view (undated) flagged a 2-4% tractor decline on high base and elevated inventory [9]. ## Where to grow
**Pursue component and implement suppliers with an OEM purchase order or approved-vendor letter, and dealers with owned premises and clean stock statements.** These borrowers ride the +10.3% output number [D] without carrying the full seasonal inventory risk. **Avoid new limits to pure seasonal dealers and to units whose only collateral is a plot in a disputed industrial area** — the governance fragmentation in [1] makes title and civic approvals slow to verify. Where a proposal lands from a supplier, check the OEM approval letter and last twelve months of invoices to that OEM; if the buyer concentration is above half of sales, ask for the OEM's payment terms in writing. ## How to grow safely
**Structure on the working-capital cycle: cash credit against stock and receivables with a drawing power recalculated monthly, and term debt only for tooling tied to a named order.** Take stock and receivable statements every month, GST returns monthly, and OEM payment advices on receipt. **Covenant on receivables days and on promoter contribution; if receivables stretch beyond the stated OEM terms, ask for the ageing and hold further disbursal.** Gearing discipline matters — a rated peer carried gearing of 3.4 times [10], so treat anything materially above that as a conversation, not a tick-box. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch dealer inventory and rabi cash flow first.** If a dealer's stock statement shows machines ageing past one season, cut drawing power and ask for a liquidation plan. If GST turnover falls two months running against the Punjab +9.7% trend [D], ask for the sales register and the OEM's dispatch schedule. If the OEM delays payment advices or a supplier's single-buyer share rises, reprice or reduce. Collect from customer the actual receivable days, inventory turns and capex plans — the sources do not give these for Mohali.
watch: Ageing beyond one season -> cut drawing power, seek liquidation plan
Two consecutive months of falling turnover -> ask for sales register and OEM dispatch schedule
Delayed or missing advices -> hold disbursal, reprice
Gearing materially above 3.4 times [10] -> require fresh contribution before enhancement
